questions.stem: A 31-year-old man is evaluated because he and his wife have not conceived after 18 months. Three years ago he was treated for Hodgkin lymphoma with chemotherapy that included an alkylating agent. He has normal libido, shaves daily, and has normal muscle mass. Both testes are slightly small and soft. Two semen analyses show no sperm. Serum testosterone is 540 ng/dL (reference 300-1,000), LH is 6 mIU/mL (reference 2-9), and FSH is 31 mIU/mL (reference 2-10). Reduced secretion of which product best explains the isolated rise in FSH?
questions.explanation: Alkylating chemotherapy destroys the rapidly dividing **germ cells**, while **Leydig cells** are more resistant, so testosterone and LH stay normal. Sertoli cells make **inhibin B** only when spermatogenesis is active, so loss of germ cells lowers inhibin B and removes its selective negative feedback on **FSH**. **Androgen-binding protein** is also a Sertoli cell product, but it keeps testosterone concentrated inside the tubules and does not signal to the pituitary. Low testosterone would raise **LH** as well, which is not the case here.
questions.explanation_pt: A quimioterapia com agente alquilante destrói as **células germinativas**, que se dividem rapidamente, enquanto as **células de Leydig** são mais resistentes; por isso a testosterona e o LH continuam normais. As células de Sertoli produzem **inibina B** apenas quando a espermatogênese está ativa, então a perda de células germinativas reduz a inibina B e retira seu feedback negativo seletivo sobre o **FSH**. A **proteína ligadora de andrógenos** também vem das células de Sertoli, mas ela mantém a testosterona concentrada nos túbulos e não sinaliza para a hipófise. Uma testosterona baixa elevaria também o **LH**, o que não acontece aqui.

questions.stem: A 25-year-old man comes to the clinic because he is still growing taller and has knee pain. He is 204 cm tall, and his arm span is 214 cm. He has a full beard, a normal adult penis and normal-sized, firm testes. A hand x-ray shows open growth plates, and bone densitometry shows low bone mass. Serum testosterone is 1,150 ng/dL (reference 300-1,000), LH is 12 mIU/mL (reference 2-9), FSH is 18 mIU/mL (reference 2-10), and estradiol is undetectable (reference 10-40 pg/mL). Deficiency of which enzyme best explains these findings?
questions.explanation: **Aromatase** turns testosterone into **estradiol**, and in men estradiol is the signal that **closes the growth plates** and maintains bone mass; it also supplies part of the negative feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary. Without it, he keeps growing with **eunuchoid proportions** and osteopenia, estradiol is absent, and LH, FSH and testosterone are often high. In **5α-reductase deficiency** the external genitalia are ambiguous at birth, and estradiol is normal, so the epiphyses close on time. Normal-sized testes and normal virilization exclude primary testicular failure as the cause of his tall stature.
questions.explanation_pt: A **aromatase** transforma testosterona em **estradiol**, e no homem é o estradiol que **fecha as placas de crescimento** e mantém a massa óssea; ele também responde por parte do feedback negativo sobre o hipotálamo e a hipófise. Sem ela, o crescimento continua, com **proporções eunucoides** e osteopenia, o estradiol fica ausente e LH, FSH e testosterona costumam ficar altos. Na **deficiência de 5α-redutase** a genitália externa é ambígua ao nascimento e o estradiol é normal, então as epífises se fecham no tempo esperado. Testículos de tamanho normal e virilização normal excluem falência testicular primária como causa da estatura alta.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man had a vasectomy 7 years ago and a surgical reversal 1 year ago. He and his new partner have not conceived. Semen analysis shows a normal sperm count, but many sperm are stuck together head-to-head and motility is poor. Testing finds antibodies bound to the sperm surface. In an intact testis, which structure normally keeps the immune system away from the developing germ cells that carry these antigens?
choices: Basement membrane of the seminiferous tubule
Leydig cell clusters in the interstitium
questions.explanation: Germ cells that enter meiosis make **new surface antigens** after immune tolerance was set, so they must be hidden. **Tight junctions between neighboring Sertoli cells** form the **blood-testis barrier** and separate the basal compartment from the **adluminal compartment**, where spermatocytes and spermatids develop. A vasectomy lets sperm leak out of the blocked duct, the immune system meets these antigens, and **antisperm antibodies** cause clumping and poor motility. The **peritubular myoid cells** and the **basement membrane** lie outside the spermatogonia and only partly restrict passage; they are not the main barrier.
questions.explanation_pt: As células germinativas que entram em meiose expressam **antígenos de superfície novos**, surgidos depois que a tolerância imune já estava formada, por isso precisam ficar escondidas. As **junções de oclusão entre células de Sertoli vizinhas** formam a **barreira hematotesticular** e separam o compartimento basal do **compartimento adluminal**, onde se desenvolvem espermatócitos e espermátides. Na vasectomia, espermatozoides extravasam do ducto obstruído, o sistema imune encontra esses antígenos e os **anticorpos antiespermatozoides** causam aglutinação e baixa motilidade. As **células mioides peritubulares** e a **membrana basal** ficam por fora das espermatogônias e só restringem parcialmente a passagem; não são a barreira principal.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man with azoospermia has normal serum testosterone, LH and FSH. Imaging shows no blockage of the genital ducts. A testicular biopsy shows maturation arrest: no spermatids or spermatozoa are present. Chromosome analysis of the most advanced germ cells shows that each cell has 23 chromosomes, and every chromosome still has two sister chromatids. At which stage are these cells?
questions.explanation: **Meiosis I** separates homologous chromosomes, so its product, the **secondary spermatocyte**, has **23 chromosomes** that are each still made of **two sister chromatids** (1N, 2C: haploid chromosome number, double DNA content). **Meiosis II** then splits the chromatids to make spermatids with 23 single-chromatid chromosomes. A **primary spermatocyte** is the tempting choice, but it still has **46 duplicated chromosomes** (2N, 4C) because it has not finished meiosis I. Spermatogonia are diploid cells that divide by mitosis.
questions.explanation_pt: A **meiose I** separa os cromossomos homólogos, então seu produto, o **espermatócito secundário**, tem **23 cromossomos**, cada um ainda formado por **duas cromátides-irmãs** (1N, 2C: número haploide de cromossomos, conteúdo de DNA duplicado). A **meiose II** então separa as cromátides e forma espermátides com 23 cromossomos de cromátide única. O **espermatócito primário** é a alternativa tentadora, mas ainda tem **46 cromossomos duplicados** (2N, 4C), pois não terminou a meiose I. As espermatogônias são células diploides que se dividem por mitose.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man had a radical prostatectomy for localized prostate cancer 8 months ago. Since then he has had no erections, including on waking. Penile sensation is normal, and he can reach orgasm, although no fluid comes out. Serum testosterone is normal. Sildenafil taken before sexual activity has not helped. Which mechanism best explains why the drug did not work?
choices: Loss of nitric oxide release from cavernous nerve endings
Increased PDE-5 activity in cavernosal smooth muscle
Loss of pudendal motor input to the ischiocavernosus muscle
Excess α1-adrenergic tone in cavernosal smooth muscle
Loss of sensory input from the dorsal nerve of the penis
questions.explanation: The **cavernous nerves** carry **parasympathetic** fibers from **S2-S4** and run in the neurovascular bundles beside the prostate, where they are often injured during radical prostatectomy. Erection starts when these nerves release **nitric oxide**, which activates guanylyl cyclase to make **cGMP** and relax cavernosal smooth muscle. **Sildenafil** only slows cGMP breakdown by **PDE-5**, so with little NO there is little cGMP to protect. More PDE-5 activity would be overcome by the drug, and normal penile sensation shows that the somatic **dorsal nerve** is intact.
questions.explanation_pt: Os **nervos cavernosos** levam fibras **parassimpáticas** de **S2-S4** e passam nos feixes neurovasculares ao lado da próstata, onde frequentemente são lesados na prostatectomia radical. A ereção começa quando esses nervos liberam **óxido nítrico**, que ativa a guanilato ciclase para produzir **GMPc** e relaxar a musculatura lisa cavernosa. A **sildenafila** apenas retarda a degradação do GMPc pela **PDE-5**, então com pouco NO há pouco GMPc para proteger. Um aumento da atividade da PDE-5 seria superado pelo fármaco, e a sensibilidade peniana normal mostra que o **nervo dorsal** somático está íntegro.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old man has had type 1 diabetes for 25 years, with gastroparesis and dizziness on standing. For the past year he has had orgasms with almost no fluid coming out. His erections are adequate. A urine sample collected right after orgasm is cloudy; microscopy shows many sperm, and fructose is present. Failure of which process best explains his symptoms?
choices: Contraction of the vas deferens and seminal vesicles
Rhythmic contraction of the bulbospongiosus muscle
Liquefaction of semen by prostatic proteases
Closure of the bladder neck during emission
questions.explanation: Sperm and fructose in post-orgasm urine mean that semen did reach the posterior urethra but flowed **backward into the bladder**: **retrograde ejaculation**. During emission, **sympathetic α1-adrenergic** fibers close the **internal urethral sphincter (bladder neck)**; diabetic **autonomic neuropathy** (also suggested by gastroparesis and orthostatic dizziness) prevents this closure. Failure of **emission** itself is the tempting choice, but then no sperm or seminal vesicle fructose would reach the urine at all. Weak **bulbospongiosus** contraction would make semen dribble out of the penis rather than enter the bladder.
questions.explanation_pt: Espermatozoides e frutose na urina após o orgasmo indicam que o sêmen chegou à uretra posterior, mas voltou **para a bexiga**: **ejaculação retrógrada**. Durante a emissão, fibras **simpáticas α1-adrenérgicas** fecham o **esfíncter uretral interno (colo vesical)**; a **neuropatia autonômica** diabética (sugerida também pela gastroparesia e pela tontura ao ortostatismo) impede esse fechamento. A falha da própria **emissão** é a alternativa tentadora, mas nesse caso nem espermatozoides nem a frutose das vesículas seminais chegariam à urina. Uma contração fraca do **bulboesponjoso** faria o sêmen escorrer pelo pênis, e não entrar na bexiga.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old man has fatigue, low libido and weaker erections for 2 years. His BMI is 42 kg/m2. He has mild bilateral breast enlargement, and both testes are normal in size. He takes no medications or supplements. Morning labs show total testosterone 210 ng/dL (reference 300-1,000) with a low free testosterone, LH 2.5 mIU/mL (reference 2-9), FSH 3 mIU/mL (reference 2-10), estradiol 58 pg/mL (reference 10-40) and a normal prolactin. Which mechanism best explains his low testosterone?
choices: Primary failure of the Leydig cells
Estradiol feedback suppressing GnRH and LH
Rapid conversion of testosterone to DHT in the skin
Resistance of the Leydig cells to LH
questions.explanation: Excess **adipose tissue** contains a lot of **aromatase**, which turns androgens into **estradiol**. The high estradiol feeds back on the hypothalamus and pituitary, so GnRH and **LH stay low-normal** despite a low testosterone: a **secondary (hypogonadotropic)** pattern, and the estradiol also explains the breast enlargement. **Primary Leydig cell failure** or **LH resistance** would remove feedback and make LH **high**. Prolactin is normal, so it is not suppressing GnRH.
questions.explanation_pt: O excesso de **tecido adiposo** contém muita **aromatase**, que transforma andrógenos em **estradiol**. O estradiol alto exerce feedback sobre o hipotálamo e a hipófise, então o GnRH e o **LH ficam normais-baixos** apesar da testosterona baixa: um padrão **secundário (hipogonadotrófico)**; o estradiol também explica o aumento das mamas. Uma **falência primária das células de Leydig** ou uma **resistência ao LH** retiraria o feedback e deixaria o LH **alto**. A prolactina é normal, então não está suprimindo o GnRH.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man is evaluated for infertility. Semen analysis shows a volume of 2.8 mL, a normal sperm count, and a pH of 8.4 (reference 7.2-8.0). The sample is still a thick gel after 60 minutes at room temperature, and sperm motility is low. Fructose is normal, but citrate, zinc and acid phosphatase are all low. Reduced secretion from which structure best explains these results?
questions.explanation: The **prostate** adds a slightly acidic fluid rich in **citrate**, **zinc** and **acid phosphatase**, plus **PSA**, a protease that breaks down the semen clot so the sample **liquefies** within 15 to 30 minutes. With little prostatic fluid, the clot does not liquefy, sperm stay trapped, and the alkaline seminal vesicle fluid raises the pH. The **seminal vesicles** are the tempting choice, but they make the clotting proteins and the **fructose**, which is normal here, and their loss would lower both volume and pH.
questions.explanation_pt: A **próstata** acrescenta um fluido levemente ácido, rico em **citrato**, **zinco** e **fosfatase ácida**, além do **PSA**, uma protease que desfaz o coágulo seminal para que a amostra se **liquefaça** em 15 a 30 minutos. Com pouco fluido prostático, o coágulo não se liquefaz, os espermatozoides ficam presos e o fluido alcalino das vesículas seminais eleva o pH. As **vesículas seminais** são a alternativa tentadora, mas elas produzem as proteínas do coágulo e a **frutose**, que aqui está normal, e sua ausência reduziria o volume e o pH.
